title: Bad JSON number: verified cause, minimal fix
scenario: An error dialog names a real config.json whose line 3 has "port": 80x80.
expected: verified=True, cause names line 3; fix is edit_file on that file replacing a text that occurs exactly once; applying it gives valid JSON equal to the intended config.

title: Bad JSON with no safe fix: no fix invented
scenario: The named config.json misses a comma between two keys.
expected: verified=True with the line of the error; fix is None.

title: Named file is valid now: no claim
scenario: The dialog names config.json, which parses fine now.
expected: verified=False, fix None, evidence says 'valid JSON now', the dialog text is not put in the cause.

title: Named file does not exist
scenario: The dialog names a config.json path that does not exist.
expected: verified=False and fix None.

title: Port in use, checked against the real listener
scenario: A real socket listens on a port; the dialog says that port is in use and names the app's config.json.
expected:
verified=True naming this process's pid; fix replaces exactly '"port":

' with a port that is really free (bind succeeds).

title: Port claimed in use but nothing listens
scenario: The listener was closed before the diagnosis.
expected: verified=False, 'hypothesis' in the cause, fix None.

title: Disk really too full
scenario: The dialog says it needs 999999999 MB on the system drive; the real free space is checked.
expected: verified=True, needs_mb recorded, fix None, advice leaves deleting to the owner.

title: Low-space claim the disk contradicts
scenario: The dialog says it needs 1 MB on the system drive, which has far more free.
expected: verified=False with 'hypothesis' in the cause and no fix.

title: Low space on a drive that does not exist
scenario: The dialog names drive Q: (absent on Linux).
expected: verified=False, 'could not be checked' in the cause, never 'None MB'.

title: Service down, checked
scenario: The dialog says connection refused at 127.0.0.1:<a free port>.
expected: verified=True 'nothing is listening', fix None, advice to start the service.

title: Missing DLL, really absent
scenario: 'JARVISRuntime140.dll was not found'; neither the app folder nor PATH has it.
expected: verified=True, dependency JARVISRuntime140.dll, fix None.

title: Missing DLL that is present after all
scenario: The same message, but the DLL exists in the app folder.
expected: verified=False, the cause is labelled a hypothesis, evidence 'present after all'.

title: Missing Python module stays a hypothesis
scenario: Traceback 'No module named sample_lib' (its environment is not checked).
expected: verified=False, 'hypothesis' in the cause, dependency named.

title: Crash record alone is a hypothesis
scenario: No dialog; one Application Error event and a crash record (ucrtbase.dll, c0000409).
expected: verified=False, 'hypothesis' in the cause, evidence lists the crash record and the event count.

title: Nothing wrong found
scenario: Only the app's normal window, no events, no crashes.
expected: verified=False, cause starts 'no error dialog', fix None.

title: Repair backs up before writing
scenario: repair.edit_file on a real config.json in the user's folder.
expected: ok and verified_on_disk; the backup equals the original bytes and its manifest sha256 matches; undo command given.

title: Restore undoes, and can itself be undone
scenario: edit_file, then restore(backup), then restore(the restore's undo).
expected: Original text back after the restore; the fixed value back after undoing the restore.

title: Refused repairs change nothing
scenario: Ambiguous find (2 matches), empty find, /etc/hostname, a file in the backups folder, restore id '../../etc'.
expected: All refused; '2 times' in the ambiguous error; the config bytes unchanged; no backup written.

title: Tampered backup is not restored
scenario: The backup file is overwritten after the edit, then restore is asked.
expected: Refused with 'does not match'; the current file is left as it is.

title: Protected programs are never restarted
scenario: restart_app for lsass, KeePass, jarvis_node and 'a;b' (PowerShell and process start faked).
expected: All 4 refused; no script run and nothing started.

title: App asking to save is not forced
scenario: restart_app: the program did not close within 8 s (unsaved work prompt).
expected: ok=False with 'NOT forced'; it is not started again.

title: Restart not claimed without the check
scenario: restart_app: closed and started again, but the after-check says not responding.
expected: ok=False, running True, responding False, 'not running and answering' in the error.

title: Restart that passes its check
scenario: restart_app: closed, started from the same path, the after-check says running and responding.
expected: ok=True; started once from the recorded path; the CHECK script ran.

title: Install not listed afterwards is not success
scenario: repair.install with winget faked: the install was cancelled at UAC and 'winget list' does not show it; plus an injected id.
expected: ok=False (listed_after False) after one install and one list call; 'x && calc' refused.

title: Repairs need the owner's approval
scenario: Kernel policy for repair actions: edit config.json, restart, install, restore, edit settings.json, edit a secrets file, uninstall.
expected: YELLOW_APPROVAL, YELLOW_APPROVAL, YELLOW_APPROVAL, YELLOW_AUTO, RED, DENY, RED.

title: Troubleshooter: approved fix, verified by restart
scenario: run_troubleshooter against a fake console over local HTTP: the app's error dialog names its config.json (80x80); the owner approves; the node's real repair runs; OK is pressed; the app is started again.
expected: Outcome 'fixed and verified'; 1 approval asked, 1 repair; port 8080 on disk; 0 error dialogs after; backup equals the original; waiting_for_permission in the steps; no local screen-text file left.

title: Troubleshooter: denied fix changes nothing
scenario: The same, but the owner denies the approval.
expected: Outcome starts 'not approved'; the config bytes unchanged; no repair ran; no backup made.

title: Troubleshooter: fix applied but the error stays
scenario: The config has two faults (80x80 on line 3, 30s on line 4); the approved fix repairs the first; the app still shows its error after restart.
expected: Outcome starts 'fix applied, but the check failed'; exactly 1 repair (no repair loop); 1 error dialog seen after; undo offered.

title: Failed repair step is not re-run
scenario: Coordinator: a troubleshoot step reports 'fix applied, but the check failed' with a timeout error.
expected: The troubleshooter runs once (no second repair), task 'failed', no 'Done'.

title: Crash announced once, also after a restart
scenario: Monitor sees a crash event, saves its state, restarts from it, then a new hang event arrives.
expected: 1 crash alert; 0 alerts for the same event after the restart; 1 'stopped responding' alert for the new one.

title: Service down needs two failed checks
scenario: A service that answered before fails one check, then a second, then a third.
expected: 0 alerts after one, 1 alert naming port 8080 after two, 0 after three (no repeat).

title: Real crash diagnosed from the Windows event log
scenario: On the laptop: JARVISCrashCanary.exe crashes; the troubleshooter reads events 1000/1002 and the crash record.
expected: Crash record with module and code in the evidence; cause labelled a hypothesis; nothing changed.

title: Real restart of a Windows app
scenario: On the laptop: restart_app on the sample app via CloseMainWindow and a fresh start.
expected: Never forced; success only when the process runs and responds after the restart.

title: winget install through the UAC prompt
scenario: On the laptop: an approved install of a small package; the owner answers the UAC prompt.
expected: Success only when 'winget list' shows the package afterwards; a cancelled UAC is reported as not installed.

title: Same typo twice: no fix that cannot apply
scenario: The named config.json lists two servers, each with "port": 80x80 on its own line. The proposed edit replaces one exact text, and repair.edit_file refuses a text that occurs more than once.
expected: verified=True at the first faulty line; the fix is None or its text occurs exactly once in the file.

dialog: JARVIS Sample App could not start.

title: Port in use, config holds it twice: no fix that cannot apply
scenario: A real listener holds the port; the named config.json uses that port for two services ("web" and "admin").
expected: verified=True naming the listener; the fix is None or its text occurs exactly once in the file.

dialog: Port {port} is already in use by another program.

title: Port in use, port written as a string: cause verified, no fix guessed
scenario: A real listener holds the port; the named config.json stores it as "port": "<port>" (a string the number-edit pattern does not cover).
expected: verified=True with cause 'port <port> is already used by ...'; fix None.

dialog: Port {port} is already in use by another program.

title: Config cut off mid-write or empty: verified line, no fix invented
scenario: The named config.json is truncated after "port": 80 (a crash mid-write), or is a zero-byte file.
expected: verified=True at line 3 / line 1 respectively; fix None for both.

title: A URL that ends in .json is not taken as a local file
scenario: The dialog says it could not download http://updates.example.com<path>/config.json; a broken file really exists at that local <path> (so a careless match would 'verify' and 'fix' it).
expected: No file is taken from the URL; verified False; fix None.

title: Connection refused on another machine: no claim
scenario: The dialog says the service at 10.0.0.5:8080 refused the connection. Only local ports can be checked here.
expected: verified False, fix None, and the cause does not say 'nothing is listening'.

texts: Could not connect to the service at 10.0.0.5:8080 (connection refused).

title: Diagnosis survives wrong-typed node output
scenario: core.diagnose gets malformed input from the node: texts given as one string, a null window, events as an object instead of a list, a null crash record, an HTML string instead of the window list.
expected: No exception for any input; verified False and fix None each time.

title: Huge screen read: the real fault is still found, in time
scenario: 5000 ordinary windows (about 2.7 MB of text) and, at the end, the error dialog naming a broken config.json.
expected: verified at line 3 with the 8080 fix, in under 3 s.

title: Troubleshooter: malformed screen read changes nothing
scenario: The fake console (standing in for the kernel and the laptop node; the node's real repair code behind it) returns the window_text result as an HTML error page, as cut-off JSON, as a JSON object, and as a list of strings.
expected: For each: run_troubleshooter answers without raising, no repair runs, the config is unchanged, the screen-text file is deleted, and the outcome never says 'fixed'.

title: Troubleshooter: empty screen read is a hypothesis, not a fix
scenario: The fake console's window_text result file is empty both times (before and after the troubleshooter starts the program).
expected: outcome 'hypothesis only', verified False; no approval asked, no repair, no screen-text file left.

title: Troubleshooter: malformed check after the fix keeps the undo
scenario: The fix is approved and the node's real repair applies it (a real backup); then the read that should verify it comes back from the fake console as an HTML page.
expected: No exception; the report names the backup and the undo command; the outcome is not 'fixed and verified'.

title: Console port answers HTML: a clean error, not a crash
scenario: Something else listens on the console's port (a fake web server answering 200 with an HTML page to every request).
expected: core.Pc.run raises DesktopError (console not answering properly), never a JSON decode error; the troubleshooter returns Err instead of raising.

title: Coordinator: a non-object step result is a failed step
scenario: A fake agent returns an HTML string, a list, a number instead of the result object.
expected: No exception; status not completed; summary not 'Done'; the PC-task lock is released; the record is saved.

title: Coordinator: an empty step result is a failed step
scenario: A fake agent returns null, an empty object, or {"ok": null}.
expected: Status failed; summary 'I could not finish ...'; lock released; record saved.

title: Coordinator: ok given as the text 'false' is not success
scenario: A fake agent's result says {"ok": "false"} or {"ok": "no"} (a node that serialised its flag as text).
expected: Status not completed; summary not 'Done'.

title: Repair re-checks the file: an outdated fix changes nothing
scenario: Diagnosis proposes '80x80 -> 8080'; before the approved repair runs, the owner edits the file by hand (port 9090).
expected: repair.run refuses ('occurs 0 times'); the owner's file is byte-identical; no backup is made.

title: Repair is minimal: BOM, CRLF and other bytes kept
scenario: A config with a UTF-8 BOM, CRLF line ends and non-ASCII text gets the '80x80 -> 8080' edit.
expected: Only those bytes change; BOM and every CRLF kept; same line count; the backup equals the original byte for byte.

title: Repair refuses files it cannot edit safely
scenario: edit_file on a UTF-16 file, a file over the 2 MB limit, a symlink in the owner's folder pointing to a writable file outside it (holding the very text to replace), and a folder.
expected: All refused; nothing on disk changes (including the outside file); no backup is written.

title: Restore refuses a damaged backup record
scenario: The backup's manifest.json is cut off mid-write, empty, or lacks its sha256.
expected: restore() returns ok False for each; the live file stays as it is.

title: Restore refuses a wrong-typed backup record
scenario: The backup's manifest.json is valid JSON of the wrong shape: a list, a path that is a number, a sha256 that is a number.
expected: restore() returns ok False for each without raising; the live file stays as it is.

title: Restart: unreadable PowerShell answers start nothing
scenario: Fake PowerShell (a Windows program): the close step answers an HTML page, nothing, or cut-off JSON; or the close is clean and the check answers an HTML page or nothing.
expected: Never ok; the program is started only after a clean close; the restart is never claimed without a readable check.

title: Restart: a JSON list from PowerShell is refused, not a crash
scenario: Fake PowerShell's close step answers a JSON array (as ConvertTo-Json does for two objects) instead of one object.
expected: restart_app returns ok False without raising; nothing is started.

title: Install: only the exact package id counts as installed
scenario: Fake winget (a Windows program). After the install, 'winget list' shows only JARVIS.SampleApp.Beta; or exits 1 with an error that echoes the id; or exits 1 with an empty listing; control: it lists JARVIS.SampleApp exactly.
expected: ok False for the first three, ok True only for the exact listing.

title: Monitor: damaged state file does not replay old crashes
scenario: The monitor's state file is cut off mid-write; the (fake) event log holds 100 old crash records; then one new crash. A PC-task folder holds one damaged record and one task stuck for over an hour.
expected: 0 alerts on the first check after loading, 1 alert for the new crash; the damaged task record is skipped and the stuck task is announced once.

title: Node result paths outside local-only are refused, nothing deleted
scenario: A node result's local_result points outside outputs/local-only: an absolute path to another file, a ../ escape, and a link inside local-only that leads to that file. take_local() reads such a file once and DELETES it.
expected: All three refused with DesktopError and the outside file still exists; a proper file inside local-only is read and deleted.
